#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# CHECK: the runtime stage's @secuura/shared re-link, and the dev-tree it ships
# (KS-921, with the sibling assertion proposed on KS-490)
# =============================================================================
# `@secuura/shared` is a HAND-MADE, UNDECLARED symlink: every Dockerfile that
# consumes the `shared-builder` stage creates `node_modules/@secuura/shared ->
# /shared` itself. Nothing in any package.json declares it, so nothing but this
# check can notice when a stage stops creating it.
#
# It has already failed. PR #851's second commit exists BECAUSE it failed:
# `npm prune --omit=dev` in a builder removes the undeclared symlink, and three
# runtime stages that copied that pruned tree without re-creating the link
# shipped images which crashed on start with
#     Cannot find module '@secuura/shared/crypto/hybrid-kem'
# governance re-linked; nft-certificate, referral and staking did not. Nothing
# detected it — a reviewer reading four Dockerfiles side by side did.
#
# TWO ASSERTIONS, DELIBERATELY SEPARATE (see "RED-PROOF" below):
#
#   A (BLOCKING) — the re-link invariant.
#       In the FINAL stage of every Dockerfile that consumes `shared-builder`,
#       an `ln -s /shared node_modules/@secuura/shared` must appear AFTER the
#       last instruction in that stage which writes node_modules (a
#       `COPY --from=… …node_modules…`, or a dependency install) and BEFORE the
#       stage's first `USER`.
#
#       Stated over "the last thing that writes node_modules" rather than "the
#       COPY", because this repo has TWO runtime shapes and both need the link:
#       some Dockerfiles COPY a builder's node_modules, the rest re-install their
#       own with `npm ci --omit=dev`. A fresh install has no @secuura/shared
#       either. The split is DERIVED and printed in the summary — no figure here,
#       because the hand-written one ("5 and 20") had already drifted from the
#       derived one (4 and 21) in this very header, under a banner that forbids
#       exactly that.
#       KS-921's text names only the COPY shape; the wider statement is a
#       superset of it and is green on the whole class today.
#
#   B (REPORT-ONLY) — the KS-490 dev-tree invariant.
#       The node_modules that reaches the final stage must be dev-pruned: the
#       final stage's own install carries `--omit=dev`, or the builder stage it
#       copies node_modules from runs `npm prune --omit=dev`.
#
#       REPORT-ONLY, not blocking: a guard that goes in red teaches everyone to
#       ignore the guard. It becomes blocking in a later round once the class is
#       clean. Set SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1 to make it blocking (the test suite
#       does exactly that, so B's own red-proof still asserts an exit code).
#
# NO HARD-CODED CENSUS. Every figure this script prints — the size of the class,
# how many files are in each runtime shape, the per-stage install counts — is
# DERIVED from the parse. A hand-maintained number is what drifted in #849's
# commit body ("24 enumerated, 20 already omit dev"; the class is 25, because
# connectors/whatsapp-bot is not under services/).
#
# RED-PROOF — each assertion is proved INDEPENDENTLY, with the other clause
# green in the same batch. A multi-clause guard proved with one fixture that
# trips both clauses has measured the pair and learned nothing about the parts.
# Both fixtures are in scripts/__tests__/check_shared_relink.test.sh:
#   · A alone: the real tree at d602a1536 — A reds on exactly nft-certificate,
#     referral and staking; B is green there (all four builders prune).
#   · B alone: governance at develop with its `npm prune --omit=dev` removed —
#     B reds, A stays green.
#
# USAGE
#   check-shared-relink.sh [DEV_DIR]
# DEV_DIR defaults to this script's parent (Blockchain/Dev). It is an argument
# so the red-proof can point the guard at a scratch tree materialised with
# `git show`, rather than checking a historical commit out over a live worktree.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

DEV_DIR="${1:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)}"
cd "$DEV_DIR"

STRICT="${SHARED_RELINK_STRICT:-0}"

EXIT=0
b_failures=0
exempt_count=0
copy_shape=0

# The class is DERIVED: every Dockerfile that consumes the shared-builder stage.
#
# The two steps are separate on purpose. `grep -l PATTERN $(find ...)` with an
# empty find result has NO file operands, so grep falls back to STDIN and blocks
# — and this runs from the pre-push hook, whose stdin is the ref list git is
# feeding it. An empty corpus has to be detected before grep is invoked, not by
# the shape of its output.
ALL_DOCKERFILES=$(find . -name Dockerfile -not -path '*/node_modules/*' 2>/dev/null | sort)
if [ -z "$ALL_DOCKERFILES" ]; then
  echo "::error::no Dockerfile at all under $DEV_DIR — this is not a tree this guard can check, and reporting clean over zero files is the vacuous green the gate exists to prevent"
  exit 1
fi

# KS-921 F-1. `-i` is load-bearing, not tidiness. Dockerfile instruction keywords
# are case-INSENSITIVE by specification, so `Copy --from=shared-builder` is a
# valid, ordinary authoring slip — and a case-sensitive selector drops that file
# out of the CLASS rather than failing it. The guard then prints
# `OK — 1 Dockerfile(s) … 1 of 1 clean` over a corpus of two whose second file is
# broken in both clauses, at rc 0, and it does so under SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1
# as well. Reproduced before it was fixed.
#
# That is this guard committing KS-921's own defect with the guard installed and
# green, and the empty-corpus refusal below could not catch it: that fires only
# when the class is ENTIRELY empty, and every derived figure shrinks in step with
# a partial miss, so nothing looks wrong.
DOCKERFILES=$(grep -l -i -E '^[[:space:]]*COPY[[:space:]].*--from=shared-builder' \
              $ALL_DOCKERFILES </dev/null 2>/dev/null | sort || true)

if [ -z "$DOCKERFILES" ]; then
  echo "::error::no Dockerfile in $DEV_DIR consumes the shared-builder stage — the class is empty, which is itself the finding"
  exit 1
fi

# THE CROSS-CHECK, and it is the real protection: a SECOND, deliberately looser
# instrument for the class size. `-i` fixes the one miss we found; the cross-check
# is what notices the next one. Any file that mentions `shared-builder` at all but
# does not match the precise selector is reported by name and fails the run — a
# narrow selector must never be able to shrink this corpus quietly.
#
# It fails LOUDLY rather than warning, on purpose: a false block is visible and
# takes one commit to resolve, a false clean is neither. If a file legitimately
# mentions the stage without consuming it, that is a real divergence between two
# readings of the same corpus and it should be settled in the guard, not assumed.
LOOSE=$(grep -l -i -F -e 'shared-builder' $ALL_DOCKERFILES </dev/null 2>/dev/null | sort || true)
divergent=$(comm -13 <(printf '%s\n' "$DOCKERFILES") <(printf '%s\n' "$LOOSE") || true)
if [ -n "$divergent" ]; then
  echo "::error::the class selector and the cross-check disagree about the corpus. These file(s) mention \`shared-builder\` but did not match \`COPY … --from=shared-builder\`:"
  printf '%s\n' "$divergent" | sed 's/^/::error::  /'
  echo "::error::A file that leaves the class SILENTLY is the KS-921 defect happening to this guard. Either it is a shape the selector must learn, or the mention is not a consumption — decide which, in the guard."
  exit 1
fi

for f in $DOCKERFILES; do
  # awk emits one verdict record per file:
  #   A_OK | A_FAIL <reason>
  #   B_OK <how> | B_FAIL <reason>
  #   INFO <shape> <final-stage install count> <total stages>
  verdict=$(awk '
    function note(k, v) { printf "%s %s\n", k, v }

    BEGIN { stage = 0; ord = 0; acc = "" }

    {
      line = $0
      sub(/\r$/, "", line)
      t = line
      sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", t)
      sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", t)

      # Dockerfile comments are WHOLE-LINE only — an inline # is command text,
      # not a comment. Skipping them here is what stops a commented-out
      # `# RUN npm ci` from being counted as an install.
      if (t ~ /^#/) next

      if (t == "") { if (acc != "") { process(acc); acc = "" } ; next }

      if (acc != "") acc = acc " " t; else acc = t
      if (acc ~ /\\$/) { sub(/\\$/, "", acc); next }
      process(acc); acc = ""
    }

    # KS-945. Answers one question: does this RUN line invoke a package manager in a
    # verb that is not known to be read-only? Separators are flattened first so a
    # manager invoked after && or ; or a pipe is seen, and the manager name is matched
    # as a WHOLE TOKEN, which is what makes `mynpm` not a package manager and stops
    # `pnpm i` from being caught by an npm rule that happens to match inside it.
    function pm_writes(L,   t, n, a, i, verb, segs, sg, k) {
      t = L
      sub(/^RUN[ \t]+/, "", t)
      # Segment on shell separators, then look ONLY at the leading word of each
      # segment. A manager name has to be in COMMAND POSITION to be an invocation:
      # `apk add --no-cache nodejs npm` installs the npm BINARY and writes no
      # node_modules, and an earlier version of this function counted that trailing
      # token as a write. It was caught by a cell that started failing on the wrong
      # CLAUSE while still exiting 1 — the exit code alone would have hidden it.
      gsub(/[;&|()]/, "\n", t)
      segs = split(t, sg, /\n/)
      for (k = 1; k <= segs; k++) {
        n = split(sg[k], a, /[ \t]+/)
        i = 1
        # step over a leading env assignment or sudo, which precede the command
        while (i <= n && (a[i] == "" || a[i] == "sudo" || a[i] ~ /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/)) i++
        if (i > n) continue
        if (a[i] != "npm" && a[i] != "yarn" && a[i] != "pnpm") continue
        verb = (i < n) ? a[i+1] : ""
        # A version or help PROBE is a flag in verb position that writes nothing:
        # `npm --version`, `node -v && npm -v`, `pnpm -h`. Before this line they fell
        # into the default-verb rule below and BLOCKED, a false block this inversion
        # introduced (rc 0 on the enumerating base, rc 1 after; found in the #879
        # review by Peter, 2026-09-08). The match is EXACT and sits AHEAD of the
        # default-verb rule, so every OTHER leading flag still runs the default verb
        # and still blocks: `yarn --frozen-lockfile` is an install.
        if (verb ~ /^(-v|--version|-h|--help)$/) continue
        # A bare manager, or one whose next token is a flag, runs its DEFAULT verb.
        # For yarn that default IS install, and the other two error out harmlessly —
        # so treating all three as a write is the fail-closed reading of the same shape.
        if (verb == "" || verb ~ /^-/) return 1
        # Read-only verbs. Anything not named here counts as a write ON PURPOSE.
        # `audit` is absent because `npm audit fix` writes; `prune` is absent because
        # it removes from node_modules and would take an unreferenced symlink with it.
        if (verb ~ /^(ls|list|view|info|show|config|ping|whoami|outdated|pack|version|help|search|docs|why|explain|team|owner|dist-tag|root|prefix|bin)$/) continue
        # `init` is the one verb worth splitting rather than guessing, because npm
        # documents `npm init <package-spec>` as the same thing as
        # `npx create-<package-spec>` — it downloads and runs a package. So bare
        # `npm init` and `npm init -y` write nothing, while `npm init foo` installs.
        # The next token decides, which costs one line and avoids BOTH a false block
        # on the common form and a false clean on the installing one.
        if (verb == "init") {
          if (i + 2 > n) continue
          if (a[i+2] ~ /^-/) continue
          return 1
        }
        return 1
      }
      return 0
    }

    function process(L,   nm, dest, u, kw) {
      ord++

        # KS-937 F-A / KS-930 F-3, the THIRD axis on which this parser fails to see a
        # node_modules write it should see. Docker instruction keywords are
        # case-INSENSITIVE; every clause below matched them case-sensitively, so a
        # lowercase `copy --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules` after the
        # re-link returned rc 0 "1 of 1 clean" — the #851 outage shape, certified.
        # KS-921 F-1 fixed the SHELL selectors that choose the corpus and did not
        # reach the awk parser they feed, which is why the axis survived a fix that
        # was about exactly this.
        #
        # Only the leading keyword is upper-cased. Paths, stage names and flags are
        # case-sensitive and are left exactly as written.
        kw = L
        sub(/[ \t].*$/, "", kw)
        if (toupper(kw) ~ /^(FROM|RUN|CMD|LABEL|MAINTAINER|EXPOSE|ENV|ADD|COPY|ENTRYPOINT|VOLUME|USER|WORKDIR|ARG|ONBUILD|STOPSIGNAL|HEALTHCHECK|SHELL)$/)
          L = toupper(kw) substr(L, length(kw) + 1)

      if (L ~ /^FROM[ \t]/) {
        stage++
        # KS-930 F-6. The base image is recorded so the exemption can make a POSITIVE
        # statement about what this stage runs, rather than inferring node-free-ness
        # from what the parser failed to find.
        u = L
        sub(/^FROM[ \t]+/, "", u)
        # `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:24-alpine` put the FLAG in
        # stage_base, so every downstream read of the base image was reading
        # `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM`. Step over any leading `--flag=value`
        # tokens before taking the image reference.
        while (u ~ /^--[A-Za-z0-9-]+=/) { sub(/^--[A-Za-z0-9-]+=[^ \t]*[ \t]*/, "", u) }
        sub(/[ \t].*$/, "", u)
        stage_base[stage] = u
        seen_stage_name[tolower(u)] = seen_stage_name[tolower(u)] + 0
        nm = L
        if (nm ~ /[ \t][Aa][Ss][ \t]+[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/) {
          sub(/^.*[ \t][Aa][Ss][ \t]+/, "", nm)
          stage_name[stage] = nm
          is_stage_name[tolower(nm)] = 1
        } else stage_name[stage] = ""
        return
      }
      if (stage == 0) return

        # KS-930 F-6. Two signals recorded per stage, BOTH independent of whether the
        # clauses below manage to classify this line, because they are what will grant
        # the nginx exemption and an exemption granted by the parser inherits the
        # parsers blind spots. Measured before building it: a stage that writes no
        # node_modules and a stage whose write this parser CANNOT read produce
        # byte-identical output, so the no-write arm is two conditions wearing one
        # message and one of them is "I did not understand this stage".
        #
        # nodeish  - a raw-text read. A shape the parser cannot follow still contains
        #            the word npm or node_modules, so it fails this and stays blocked.
        #            It deliberately does NOT look for heredocs: coverage already
        #            catches those, and two clauses that catch the same file mean
        #            neither can be red-proofed alone -- the defence-in-depth trap
        #            this ticket exists to describe.
        # unclass  - a coverage read. Any logical line whose first token is not a
        #            Dockerfile instruction was not understood; heredoc bodies land
        #            here, which is why RUN <<EOT disqualifies a stage by itself.
        # Either one alone denies the exemption, and they fail in opposite directions,
        # so a cell can tell which of them judged the file.
        u = L
        sub(/[ \t].*$/, "", u)
        # KS-930 round 2, gate finding 1. The four package-manager tokens do not
        # contain the word the runtime is actually called. Measured on the round-1
        # guard: `RUN apk add --no-cache nodejs` sets nodeish NOWHERE, because
        # "nodejs" contains none of node_modules, npm, yarn or pnpm; and neither
        # does `CMD ["node", "/app/dist/index.js"]` in the same stage. Six of eight
        # attack shapes landed A_EXEMPT at rc 0, and against this branch base every
        # one of the six was a REGRESSION: 306d0db92 blocked every no-nmwrite final
        # stage outright, and the round-1 head certified them clean.
        #
        # So the runtime is now matched BY NAME as well, on word boundaries so that
        # a substring inside an unrelated identifier cannot trip it.
        #
        # The base image is NOT judged here. It has its own arm, base_is_js_runtime,
        # with its own message, and one input judged by two clauses is the
        # defence-in-depth trap this whole ticket exists to describe: neither clause
        # can then be red-proofed alone.
        #
        # KS-930 ROUND 3, gate findings F1 and F2 -- the REGRESSION.
        # The round 2 boundary class `[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]` puts `-`, `.` and `_` INSIDE
        # the word-character set, so a runtime name followed by any of them was
        # invisible: `node-22`, `node22`, `node.22`, `node_22`, `nodejs-22`,
        # `node-lts`, `nodejs-current`, `nodejs-legacy` and the `nodejs.org`
        # tarball URL were all EXEMPT at round 2 and rc 1 at the base of this branch.
        # That is a regression, not a known gap. `base_is_js_runtime` below has
        # always allowed the suffix -- `^(node|nodejs|bun|deno)([0-9._-]|$)` --
        # and the trailing class here now mirrors it rather than inventing a
        # second convention. `npx` joins the tooling list for the same reason:
        # it names a runtime launcher, is in neither original token set, and was
        # rc 1 at base.
        #
        # THE BOUND, stated rather than left to be discovered: a name followed by
        # `[0-9._-]` is treated as that runtime with a version or variant suffix.
        # `node-exporter` is a Go binary and is now FALSELY BLOCKED by this rule;
        # `node-red` is caught too and is a JS runtime, so that one is correct.
        # We take the false block knowingly: this arm fails toward blocking, which
        # is visible, over exempting, which is not, and no class file reaches the
        # arm today. The false-block class as a whole is gate finding F3 and is NOT
        # fixed here -- Kam ruled this round regression-only. Both spellings are
        # pinned as cells so the choice is a measurement, not a silence.
        #
        # No guard is needed to get that, and this comment originally claimed one was.
        # A FROM line RETURNS out of the classifier about twenty lines above, in the
        # block that records stage_base, so it never reaches this statement at all.
        # A `toupper(u) != "FROM"` test was written here, and then removed once it was
        # tampered: the suite stayed 70/70 with the test defeated, because the test
        # could not change an outcome. That is the same shape as the $-refusal in
        # base_ships_no_js_runtime that this rounds own gate reported as a clause that
        # cannot fail -- reproduced, in the round that reports it, by the author.
        # KS-930 F-QA-2: record the FIRST line that tripped the arm. A message
        # that cannot quote what it matched forces the author to guess, and the
        # guard blocks every push touching Blockchain/Dev, so guessing is
        # expensive. Only the first is kept: it is the one to act on, and a list
        # would bury it.
        if (L ~ /node_modules|npm|npx|yarn|pnpm/) {
          nodeish[stage] = 1
          if (nodeish_hit[stage] == "") nodeish_hit[stage] = L
        }
        else if (L ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.-])(node|nodejs|bun|deno)([0-9._-]|[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]|$)/) {
          nodeish[stage] = 1
          if (nodeish_hit[stage] == "") nodeish_hit[stage] = L
        }
        if (toupper(u) !~ /^(FROM|RUN|CMD|LABEL|MAINTAINER|EXPOSE|ENV|ADD|COPY|ENTRYPOINT|VOLUME|USER|WORKDIR|ARG|ONBUILD|STOPSIGNAL|HEALTHCHECK|SHELL)$/)
          unclassified[stage] = unclassified[stage] + 1

      if (L ~ /^COPY[ \t]/ && L ~ /--from=/) {
        # KS-930 F-3. The JSON/exec form — `COPY --from=builder ["/app/node_modules",
        # "./node_modules"]` — is ordinary Docker and reaches this clause, but the
        # destination test below takes the LAST whitespace-separated token, which in
        # that form is `"./node_modules"]` with the bracket and quotes still attached.
        # It therefore fails `(^|/)node_modules/?$`, the write goes UNRECORDED, and a
        # clobber after the re-link is reported CLEAN — the #851 outage shape, measured
        # rc 0 "1 of 1 clean" before this line existed. Normalise the array punctuation
        # so the existing token logic sees the same fields it sees in the shell form.
        # Widening what the parser SEES can only ADD node_modules writes, never remove
        # one, so this direction fails safe: the worst case is a false block, which is
        # visible, not a false clean, which is not.
        gsub(/[][",]/, " ", L)
        # Only a WHOLE-TREE write counts. `COPY --from=builder
        # /app/node_modules/.prisma ./node_modules/.prisma` restores one
        # generated sub-path on top of an already-installed tree — it neither
        # ships the dev tree nor removes @secuura/shared, and reading it as a
        # whole-tree copy made this guard report a dev-tree failure against
        # originate that is not real. The DESTINATION decides: `./node_modules`
        # is the tree, `./node_modules/<anything>` is a path inside it.
        dest = L
        sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", dest)
        sub(/^.*[ \t]/, "", dest)
        if (dest ~ /(^|\/)node_modules\/?$/) {
          nmwrite[stage] = ord
          copies_nm[stage] = 1
          nm = L
          sub(/^.*--from=/, "", nm)
          sub(/[ \t].*$/, "", nm)
          nm_src[stage] = nm
        }
        return
      }

      if (L ~ /^RUN[ \t]/) {
        # KS-945. This test used to ENUMERATE install verbs — ci, install, i — which
        # fails OPEN: a verb nobody listed reads as "writes nothing", which is a false
        # clean, and package managers keep adding verbs. Measured on the enumerating
        # version: `npm add`, `npm it`, `npm install-test`, bare `yarn` and `pnpm add`
        # all returned rc 0 "1 of 1 clean" on the #851 clobber shape. It also had no
        # LEFT word boundary, so `pnpm i` was caught only by accident (npm matched
        # inside pnpm) and `mynpm i` — not a package manager — was falsely blocked.
        #
        # Inverted, it fails CLOSED: a RUN that invokes a package manager AT ALL counts
        # as a node_modules write unless its verb is on an explicit read-only allowlist.
        # An unknown verb now blocks, and a false block is visible and costs one commit
        # while a false clean is neither.
        #
        # `run` is deliberately NOT on the allowlist. `npm run <script>` can install
        # anything and this guard cannot read package.json scripts, so treating it as a
        # write is the only honest reading. Measured before choosing it: the 25 real
        # class files carry 50 `npm run` invocations and ZERO of them sit in a final
        # stage after the re-link, so this is inert on the corpus as it stands — and an
        # author it does bite has the correct fix available: place the re-link
        # after the script that might install.
        if (pm_writes(L)) {
          installs[stage]++
          nmwrite[stage] = ord
          copies_nm[stage] = 0
          if (L ~ /--omit=dev/ || L ~ /--production/) omit_dev[stage] = 1; else omit_dev[stage] = 0
        }
        if (L ~ /npm[ \t]+prune[ \t].*--omit=dev/) pruned_by_name[tolower(stage_name[stage])] = 1
        # KS-921 F-4. `ln -sf /shared …` (the idiomatic idempotent form) and
        # `ln -s /shared /app/node_modules/@secuura/shared` (natural under
        # WORKDIR /app) create the IDENTICAL symlink. Requiring the one literal
        # spelling rejected both as "final stage has NO re-link" — a false BLOCK
        # on clause A, which blocks today, so it was live friction on any author
        # who writes `-sf`. Accept any short-flag cluster containing `s`, and any
        # destination path ENDING at node_modules/@secuura/shared.
        if (L ~ /ln[ \t]+-[A-Za-z]*s[A-Za-z]*[ \t]+\/shared[ \t]+(\/[^ \t]*\/)?node_modules\/@secuura\/shared([ \t]|$)/) relink[stage] = ord
        return
      }

      # KS-921 F-2. Recording only the FIRST USER per stage rejected the
      # legitimate `USER root` -> create the link -> `USER app` shape, with a
      # message asserting the link "is attempted without the privileges to
      # create it" — which is false about that file: the link IS created with
      # privileges. The oracle is the EFFECTIVE user at the ordinal of the
      # re-link, so every USER is recorded and the last one before it decides.
      # (No apostrophes in this block: it sits inside a single-quoted awk
      # program, where one would end the string and break the script ~100
      # lines later, which is exactly how this comment came to be reworded.)
      if (L ~ /^USER[ \t]/) {
        nuser[stage]++
        user_ord[stage, nuser[stage]] = ord
        u = L
        sub(/^USER[ \t]+/, "", u); sub(/[ \t].*$/, "", u)
        user_val[stage, nuser[stage]] = u
      }
    }

    # ---- the base-image read the exemption rests on --------------------------
    #
    # INVERTED, deliberately, and this is the whole shape of the fix. The four
    # arms below are DENIALS, and before this change the exemption was granted by
    # the `else` that follows them — i.e. by the ABSENCE of a denial. That is
    # precisely what the comment on the exemption arm says it must never do:
    # granted on POSITIVE readings, never on the absence of a parse match. The
    # gap between that sentence and the code is the whole family:
    #
    #   KS-921  a case-sensitive corpus filter          -> narrowed
    #   KS-921  re-gate: the F-5 case axis half open    -> narrowed
    #   KS-930  F-3 substring inertness                 -> narrowed
    #   KS-930  F-6 exemption blind to ${VAR} prefixes  -> this one
    #
    # Four rounds, four spellings, one deny-list. A deny-list of image spellings
    # fails OPEN on the spelling nobody thought of — and the spelling nobody
    # thought of was `${REGISTRY_PREFIX}node:24-alpine`, which is 56 of the 79
    # FROM lines in this very repo.
    #
    # So the question is not which spellings to deny; it is which images we can
    # positively certify. An incomplete list still happens — but an incomplete
    # ALLOW-list fails CLOSED: the author gets a red naming their image and adds
    # it in a reviewed change, instead of shipping a crash-on-start image green.
    #
    # This list claims only that the image ships no JS runtime OF ITS OWN. A
    # stage that installs or copies one is caught by `nodeish` and by the
    # unclassified-line count, which are unchanged.
    # A base image this guard can positively identify AS a JavaScript runtime.
    # Kept separate from the allow-list so the caller gets the specific message
    # rather than the generic one; the allow-list below is what makes the
    # DEFAULT safe, this is what makes the common case legible.
    # KS-930 F-QA-2: quoted text is only useful without its indentation.
    function trim(t) {
      sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", t); sub(/[ \t\r]+$/, "", t); return t
    }

    function base_is_js_runtime(b,   nm) {
      nm = image_name_component(b)
      return (nm ~ /^(node|nodejs|bun|deno)([0-9._-]|$)/ || nm ~ /nodejs/)
    }

    function base_ships_no_js_runtime(b,   nm) {
      nm = image_name_component(b)
      if (nm == "") return 0
      # An unresolved ARG/ENV in the NAME is the "I could not read this" case,
      # which is the one thing the exemption must never be granted on.
      if (nm ~ /\$/) return 0
      return (nm in NON_JS_BASES)
    }

    # The NAME component of an image reference: registry and namespace stripped,
    # digest and tag removed. `${REGISTRY_PREFIX}nginx:1.27-alpine` -> `nginx`;
    # `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs22-debian12` -> `nodejs22-debian12`; `$NODE_IMAGE`
    # -> `$node_image`, which the `$` test above then refuses.
    function image_name_component(b,   s2, last) {
      s2 = b
      # A leading variable whose NAME says it is a registry prefix is stripped,
      # because a registry cannot change the image NAME: this repo writes
      # `${REGISTRY_PREFIX}node:24-alpine` on 56 of its 79 FROM lines and
      # `${REGISTRY_PREFIX}nginx:...` is the same shape for a legitimate exempt
      # stage. Refusing every `$` outright denied that one too — a false BLOCK,
      # which is the failure this guard has already been through once.
      #
      # The strip is gated on the variable NAME (REGISTRY/REPO/MIRROR/PREFIX) so
      # that `$NODE_IMAGE`, where the variable IS the reference, is NOT stripped
      # and falls to the `$` refusal below. Bounded assumption, stated: the
      # prefix carries its own trailing separator or is empty, which is how this
      # repo uses it. A variable forming part of the NAME itself would defeat
      # this read; that shape does not occur here.
      sub(/^\$\{[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(REGISTRY|REPO|MIRROR|PREFIX)[A-Za-z0-9_]*\}/, "", s2)
      sub(/^\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(REGISTRY|REPO|MIRROR|PREFIX)[A-Za-z0-9_]*/, "", s2)
      sub(/@.*$/, "", s2)
      if (match(s2, /\/[^\/]*$/)) last = substr(s2, RSTART + 1); else last = s2
      sub(/:.*$/, "", last)
      return tolower(last)
    }

    # The USER in force at ordinal `at`: the last USER declared before it. Root
    # (or no USER at all) can create the link, so only a non-root effective user
    # is a finding.
    function effective_user_is_unprivileged(st, at,   i, u) {
      u = ""
      for (i = 1; i <= nuser[st]; i++) {
        if (user_ord[st, i] < at) u = user_val[st, i]
      }
      if (u == "") return 0
      if (u == "root" || u == "0") return 0
      return 1
    }

    END {
      # Images that ship no JavaScript runtime of their own. Keep it short and
      # keep it justified: every entry is a claim someone can check by pulling
      # the image. Adding one is a reviewed change; that is the point.
      split("nginx httpd caddy alpine busybox scratch static", _njs, " ")
      for (_i in _njs) NON_JS_BASES[_njs[_i]] = 1

      if (acc != "") process(acc)
      final = stage

      # ---- assertion A: the re-link, correctly placed, in the final stage ----
      if (!(final in nmwrite)) {
        # KS-930 F-6, ruled option A. A final stage that carries no node_modules
        # CANNOT violate the re-link invariant, and before this arm existed the guard
        # offered such a stage no route to green at all: adding the re-link honestly
        # returned the SAME error, and the only passing shape was to install a node
        # tree into a static-serving image purely to satisfy the check. A guard whose
        # sole route to green degrades the artefact is not a guard.
        #
        # The exemption is granted on POSITIVE readings, never on the absence of a
        # parse match, because absence is exactly what an unreadable write looks like.
        if (nodeish[final]) {
          note("A_FAIL", "final stage writes node_modules nowhere — but this line names a JavaScript runtime or its tooling: `" trim(nodeish_hit[final]) "`" (nodeish_hit[final] == "" ? " (an open heredoc, so the stage text cannot be read line by line)" : "") ", so this guard will not certify it as node-free (unexpected shape). Matched by: node/nodejs/bun/deno, each optionally carrying a version or variant suffix — so node-22, node22, nodejs-current and node-lts all count — or the tooling tokens npm/npx/yarn/pnpm/node_modules. REMEDY: if this stage genuinely ships no JavaScript runtime, change the matched text — rename the binary or path, or move the line into a builder stage. If the match is a name that merely BEGINS with a runtime name and is not one (node-exporter is the known example), that is a stated bound of this rule, not a bug in your file: record it on the guard ticket. Do NOT reach for --no-verify — it skips all 13 preflight legs, not this one")
        } else if (base_is_js_runtime(stage_base[final])) {
          note("A_FAIL", "final stage writes node_modules nowhere — but its base image is `" stage_base[final] "`, a JavaScript runtime, so a node tree this guard cannot see (a bundled or copied one) would ship unlinked. The exemption is for stages with no node runtime at all")
        } else if (tolower(stage_base[final]) in is_stage_name) {
          note("A_FAIL", "final stage writes node_modules nowhere — but it is built FROM the earlier stage `" stage_base[final] "`, so what it inherits cannot be read from this file alone")
        } else if (!base_ships_no_js_runtime(stage_base[final])) {
          # The fail-closed default, and the reason this arm sits LAST: the two
          # arms above give a caller the specific diagnosis when we can make one.
          # This one catches everything else, which is the case the old
          # prefix-anchored regex waved through.
          note("A_FAIL", "final stage writes node_modules nowhere — but its base image `" stage_base[final] "` is not one this guard can positively identify as shipping no JavaScript runtime, so a node tree it cannot see (a bundled or copied one) would ship unlinked. Add the image to NON_JS_BASES in this file if it genuinely ships no JS runtime")
        } else if (unclassified[final] + 0 > 0) {
          note("A_FAIL", "final stage writes node_modules nowhere — but " (unclassified[final] + 0) " line(s) in it are not Dockerfile instructions this guard classifies, so it cannot claim the stage is node-free (unexpected shape)")
        } else {
          note("A_EXEMPT", "final stage writes no node_modules, copies no builder tree, mentions no node tooling, and every line in it was classified — the re-link invariant does not apply to this stage")
        }
      } else if (!(final in relink)) {
        note("A_FAIL", "final stage has NO `ln -s /shared node_modules/@secuura/shared` — a copied or freshly installed tree carries no @secuura/shared, so the image crashes on start")
      } else if (relink[final] < nmwrite[final]) {
        note("A_FAIL", "the re-link runs BEFORE the last instruction that writes node_modules — that instruction overwrites it")
      } else if (effective_user_is_unprivileged(final, relink[final])) {
        note("A_FAIL", "the re-link runs after a non-root `USER` — it is attempted without the privileges to create it")
      } else note("A_OK", "")

      # ---- assertion B: the tree that reaches the final stage is dev-pruned ----
      if (!(final in nmwrite)) {
        # KS-930 round 2, gate finding 2. This clause carried the PRE-INVERSION
        # regex verbatim, about fifteen lines below the arm the round rewrote --
        # the exact deny-list shape whose removal was the round headline, left
        # untouched and unmentioned. It disagreed with assertion A on the single
        # most common spelling in this repo: for a final stage based on
        # `${REGISTRY_PREFIX}node:24-alpine` (18 of 25 class files), one run
        # asserted BOTH "a node tree this guard cannot see would ship unlinked"
        # AND "obtains no node_modules at all", about the same stage. It could not
        # change the exit code today, because every case where B_EXEMPT was wrong
        # is a case where A already fails -- but the header states B becomes
        # blocking in a later round, and it would have arrived carrying the defect.
        #
        # Both layers now ask the same question through the same function, so the
        # two cannot drift apart again.
        if (!nodeish[final] && unclassified[final] + 0 == 0 \
            && !base_is_js_runtime(stage_base[final]) \
            && !(tolower(stage_base[final]) in is_stage_name))
          note("B_EXEMPT", "final stage obtains no node_modules at all — there is no tree to prune")
        else
          note("B_FAIL", "cannot determine how the final stage obtains node_modules")
      } else if (copies_nm[final]) {
        # KS-921 F-5, the other direction. `pruned_by_name` is keyed on
        # tolower(stage_name); looking it up with the RAW reference made
        # `AS builder` + `--from=Builder` a false B failure. Docker resolves
        # stage names case-insensitively (verified against real BuildKit: a
        # `--from=Builder` reference to a `builder` stage BUILDS), so both
        # directions must fold.
        if (tolower(nm_src[final]) in pruned_by_name)
          note("B_OK", "copies node_modules from `" nm_src[final] "`, which runs npm prune --omit=dev")
        else
          note("B_FAIL", "copies node_modules from `" nm_src[final] "`, which never runs npm prune --omit=dev — the dev tree ships into the runtime image")
      } else if (omit_dev[final]) {
        note("B_OK", "final stage installs with --omit=dev")
      } else {
        note("B_FAIL", "final stage installs WITHOUT --omit=dev — the dev tree ships into the runtime image")
      }

      note("INFO", (copies_nm[final] ? "copy-node_modules" : "reinstall") " installs_in_final=" (installs[final] + 0) " stages=" final)
    }
  ' "$f")

  a_line=$(printf '%s\n' "$verdict" | grep '^A_' || true)
  b_line=$(printf '%s\n' "$verdict" | grep '^B_' || true)
  i_line=$(printf '%s\n' "$verdict" | grep '^INFO ' | sed 's/^INFO //' || true)

  case "$a_line" in
    A_EXEMPT*)
      # Said out loud on purpose. An exemption that is silent is indistinguishable
      # from a guard that did not run, which is the class this whole ticket sits in.
      echo "::notice::$f — re-link invariant (KS-921): EXEMPT — ${a_line#A_EXEMPT }"
      exempt_count=$((exempt_count + 1))
      ;;
    A_FAIL*)
      echo "::error::$f — re-link invariant (KS-921): ${a_line#A_FAIL }"
      EXIT=1
      ;;
  esac

  case "$b_line" in
    B_EXEMPT*)
      echo "::notice::$f — dev-tree invariant (KS-490): EXEMPT — ${b_line#B_EXEMPT }"
      ;;
    B_FAIL*)
      if [ "$STRICT" = "1" ]; then
        echo "::error::$f — dev-tree invariant (KS-490): ${b_line#B_FAIL }"
        EXIT=1
      else
        echo "::warning::$f — dev-tree invariant (KS-490, report-only): ${b_line#B_FAIL }"
      fi
      b_failures=$((b_failures + 1))
      ;;
  esac

  case "$i_line" in
    copy-node_modules*) copy_shape=$((copy_shape + 1)) ;;
  esac

  if [ -n "${SHARED_RELINK_VERBOSE:-}" ]; then
    echo "  $f — $i_line"
  fi
done

count=$(printf '%s\n' "$DOCKERFILES" | grep -c . || true)

if [ "$EXIT" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ "$exempt_count" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "OK — $count Dockerfile(s) consume shared-builder; $((count - exempt_count)) re-link @secuura/shared in the final stage after the last node_modules write and before USER."
  else
    echo "OK — $count Dockerfile(s) consume shared-builder; all re-link @secuura/shared in the final stage after the last node_modules write and before USER."
  fi
  echo "     derived: $copy_shape copy a builder's node_modules, $((count - copy_shape)) re-install their own."
  # The commit that added the exemption said it is "ANNOUNCED (::notice:: plus a
  # count in the summary), never silent". The ::notice:: was real; the count was
  # not — exempt_count was incremented and never read, so a run with one exempt
  # file still closed with "all re-link @secuura/shared" and "N of N clean",
  # neither of which was true of that file. The ::notice:: scrolls above, which
  # is not where a reader looks.
  if [ "$exempt_count" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "     $exempt_count EXEMPT (final stage ships no JS runtime) — those files re-link nothing, by design."
  fi
fi

if [ "$b_failures" -gt 0 ]; then
  if [ "$STRICT" = "1" ]; then
    echo "     dev-tree (KS-490): $b_failures of $count file(s) ship an unpruned tree — BLOCKING (SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1)."
  else
    echo "     dev-tree (KS-490): $b_failures of $count file(s) ship an unpruned tree — report-only; set SHARED_RELINK_STRICT=1 to block."
  fi
elif [ "$EXIT" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "     dev-tree (KS-490): $count of $count clean."
fi

exit $EXIT

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Unit tests for check-shared-relink.sh (KS-921, and the KS-490 sibling assertion).
#
# The guard carries TWO assertions, so this suite's first duty is to prove them
# SEPARATELY. A multi-clause guard proved with one fixture that trips both
# clauses has measured the pair and learned nothing about the parts — so the two
# headline cases each red ONE clause and assert the other is GREEN in the same
# run:
#
#   · A alone — the real tree at d602a1536 (#851's pre-fix head): the re-link
#     assertion reds on exactly nft-certificate, referral and staking, and the
#     dev-tree assertion emits ZERO warnings there.
#   · B alone — governance at develop with its one `npm prune --omit=dev` line
#     removed: the dev-tree assertion reds on exactly that file, and the re-link
#     assertion stays green.
#
# Both historical fixtures are materialised with `git show` into a throwaway
# directory. Never `git checkout`: a control that mutates its subject is not a
# control, and this checkout carries other branches' work.
#
# Every synthetic case pins itself to ITS message, not merely to an exit code,
# so a broken rule cannot hide behind a working one.

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
GATE="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)/check-shared-relink.sh"
DEV_DIR="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$DEV_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

PASS=0; FAIL=0; SKIP=0
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# expect <name> <expected_exit> <dockerfile-body> [expected_substring] [env-assignment]
# The 4th argument pins the case to its own rule.
expect() {
    local name="$1" want="$2" body="$3" want_out="${4:-}" envset="${5:-}" d out got
    d=$(mktemp -d "$TMP/case.XXXXXX")
    mkdir -p "$d/services/thing"
    printf '%s\n' "$body" > "$d/services/thing/Dockerfile"
    if [ -n "$envset" ]; then
        out=$(env "$envset" bash "$GATE" "$d" 2>&1); got=$?
    else
        out=$(bash "$GATE" "$d" 2>&1); got=$?
    fi
    if [ "$got" != "$want" ]; then
        FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: $name (expected exit $want, got $got)"; echo "$out" | sed 's/^/        /'; return
    fi
    if [ -n "$want_out" ] && ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF -- "$want_out"; then
        FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: $name (exit correct, WRONG rule fired — wanted /$want_out/)"; echo "$out" | sed 's/^/        /'; return
    fi
    PASS=$((PASS+1))
}

ok() { PASS=$((PASS+1)); }
bad() { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: $1"; }

echo "check_shared_relink:"

# --- the shapes this repo actually has, both green ----------------------------

expect "re-install shape passes" 0 'FROM node:24-alpine AS shared-builder
WORKDIR /shared
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts
FROM node:24-alpine AS builder
COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts
RUN mkdir -p node_modules/@secuura && ln -s /shared node_modules/@secuura/shared
RUN npm run build
FROM node:24-alpine
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts --omit=dev
COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared
RUN mkdir -p node_modules/@secuura && ln -s /shared node_modules/@secuura/shared
USER secuura' "OK — 1 Dockerfile"

expect "copy-node_modules shape passes" 0 'FROM node:24-alpine AS shared-builder
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts
FROM node:24-alpine AS builder
COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts
RUN npm run build
RUN npm prune --omit=dev
FROM node:24-alpine
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared
RUN mkdir -p node_modules/@secuura && ln -s /shared node_modules/@secuura/shared
USER secuura' "OK — 1 Dockerfile"

# --- The suite must not EXECUTE its own case names.
#
# Learned the hard way on KS-945: a case name is interpolated into a double-quoted
# shell word at the call site, so a backtick in it is COMMAND SUBSTITUTION. Seven
# names written as `npm add`, `pnpm add`, `npm init <package-spec>` and so on ran
# those commands for real during a suite run -- npm init rewrote
# Blockchain/Dev/package.json and the managers rewrote package-lock.json. Both were
# restored from HEAD and verified byte-identical, and nothing was committed.
#
# The damage was invisible in the pass/fail column: the cells still passed. It
# surfaced only because a RED-PROOF run printed yarn and pnpm output inside its
# FAIL lines. So this check exists to make the hazard fail loudly instead of
# silently mutating the working tree.
unescaped=$(grep -n '^expect "' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | grep '`' | grep -v '\\`' || true)
if [ -n "$unescaped" ]; then
    bad "case names must escape backticks — an unescaped one is command substitution and RUNS: $unescaped"
else ok; fi

echo "  $PASS passed, $FAIL failed, $SKIP skipped"
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
